name: Current Consumption Model
description: The learner believes electric current is gradually used up as it passes through components.
prototypes: the first bulb uses some electricity so less reaches the second bulb
current becomes weaker after going through a bulb
electricity gets consumed by components

name: Proximity-to-Battery Model
description: The learner believes components physically closer to the battery receive more current or power.
prototypes: the bulb closer to the battery gets more electricity
the first bulb is brighter because it is nearer the battery
distance from the battery determines brightness

name: Constant-Current Battery Model
short: Battery always sends the same current
description: The learner believes a battery outputs a fixed current regardless of circuit resistance.
prototypes: the battery pushes the same current no matter what is connected
current is fixed by the battery
adding resistance does not change the battery current

name: Voltage-Current Conflation
short: Voltage and current are the same thing
description: The learner treats voltage and current as interchangeable quantities.
prototypes: voltage is the amount of current
more volts means the same thing as more current
current and voltage are basically identical

name: Component Uses All Current
description: The learner believes a resistor or bulb can consume all current flowing into it.
prototypes: the bulb uses all the current
nothing is left after the resistor
a component can take the electricity away

name: Sequential Arrival Model
short: Current reaches components one by one
description: The learner believes current first reaches the nearest component and only later reaches the next one.
prototypes: electricity reaches the first bulb before the second
the first bulb gets current earlier
current travels component by component and arrives later

name: Equal-Split Parallel Model
description: The learner believes current always divides equally between parallel branches, regardless of resistance.
prototypes: current splits fifty fifty in parallel
both branches always get equal current
parallel means current is divided equally

name: Global Resistance Effect Model
short: Adding resistance reduces current everywhere equally
description: The learner believes adding any resistor reduces current in every part of a circuit by the same amount.
prototypes: adding a resistor makes all currents smaller in the same way
one extra resistor reduces current everywhere equally
all branches lose the same current when resistance is added
